Which is a -- this is a practical question so that we can contact these witnesses, and to summon them, if that is necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the Defence already been in contact with these witnesses? Because you say you don't have the addresses. I am a bit surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I anticipated your question. We don't have their current addresses and we did think that if we try to take steps in the general way, to ask in New York in the UN HQ, they would have responded in God knows how many months, if they would respond at all. So that is why we didn't do this. So really, we don't know how to get in touch with these people, and we thought it would be much better to state the problem now so that the Chamber, who probably has more means at their disposal than the Defence, that perhaps maybe you can assist us in this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you interviewed them already? Have you been in contact with them already? Yes, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I may, but perhaps we should further consider this. Then it is quite surprising that you are asking for protective measures when you have not yet even met with these witnesses. That raises some other issues as well in respect of protective measures, but we will deal with that. The, I think, that the Chamber will certainly assist you if there are witnesses that can give relevant information, and you have difficulties in finding them, then, of course, the Chamber will assist as good as it can. And I take it that the Prosecution, that might have information about the whereabouts of the witnesses as well would assist the Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we would be happy to provide information, if we have it. Although I note that Mr. Piletta-Zanin has described these people as military personnel. I can tell you, Mr. President, that what we would do in that situation is simply contact the relevant military, and we haven't had a problem in the past in using that avenue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that is even, as far as the methodology is concerned, you got the first assistance already of the Prosecution, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Of course, if you asked for the assistance of the Chamber, it is important for the Chamber to note what efforts you have made up to that moment, and what route you tried to follow in order to get the information you need. But, in general terms, you can rely upon the Chamber to assist you in getting witnesses here that are relevant for your case. You said you had one or two questions, but please also keep in mind that it might need some time. So, therefore, the sooner you report what you have done in order to reach these witnesses, and what assistance you would seek, the better the Chamber and perhaps also the Prosecution would be able to assist you. This was one issue. Is there another issue you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there was a second issue, but perhaps this is a premature moment to speak about it. In order to gain time, we are going to raise it at a later stage, if there is need for it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: About the safe conduct, no safe conduct is required for any of the witnesses to appear next week or is there? Because the practical part of safe conduct is not -- it is a complicated matter, especially also in communication with all kind of authorities. So not even predicting what the decision of the Chamber will be, but I just wanted to be sure that we are not facing any problems for next week. Yes. So then we have no other items on our agenda. The decision -- yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would just like to ask the Chamber, if you can give us the information or are we going to get that from the SLO about the schedule of the trial? Is it going to be the usual, one week a.m., one week p.m.?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can see, we have a similar -- but the court calendar is prepared by the Registry, and is available, I think, up until December. So I think next week we start at the p.m. sessions. So we would start at a quarter past 2.00. But this information is available for you, yes, even holidays and court maintenance, everything is on there. So perhaps a copy of the court calendar for the next month could be provided to you so that you are well informed. Yes. Then I thank the parties for their cooperation. I think all those who assisted us both in the technical booth and the interpreters for their assistance. We will adjourn. And the decision of the Chamber on the 98 bis motion will be filed today and the -- we will adjourn until next Monday at a quarter past 2.00 in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 11.50 a.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 7th day of October, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
